title: French Fifth Republic
capsule: The French Fifth Republic was proclaimed on 4 October 1958, when a new constitution drafted under Charles de Gaulle's direction replaced the discredited Fourth Republic, substantially strengthening executive presidential power relative to parliament. De Gaulle used this authority to negotiate the 1962 Evian Accords ending the Algerian War and to withdraw France from NATO's integrated command structure. The republic endured severe domestic strain during the May 1968 student and worker uprisings, after which de Gaulle resigned (1969), but the constitutional framework itself proved durable under successive presidents from Pompidou through Chirac, Sarkozy, Hollande, and Macron. As of the dataset's attestation through 2024, the Fifth Republic continues as the governing constitutional order of France.
